title.bn: কনফিউশন ম্যাট্রিক্সে দুই রকম ভুল আলাদা করা

summary.en: Count actual-versus-predicted categories, move a fixed score threshold and read binary or multiclass confusion matrices.
summary.bn: আসল ও predicted লেবেল গুনো, স্থির score-এর threshold বদলাও এবং binary বা multiclass confusion matrix পড়ো।

sections.title: Two mistakes can have different meanings
Choose the actual row before the predicted column
Count six scored examples once each
Rebuild the counts after one policy change
Verify binary counts and inspect three-class errors
More categories add specific confusion routes
Keep labels, decisions and consequences separate
Optional: a count table before any ratio
Count the kind of mistake before choosing a metric

examples.title: Count each fixed-score decision into one cell
examples.explanationHtml: The six known labels and model scores are held fixed. At threshold 0.5, two negatives and two positives are correct, while one example lands in each error cell. Every card contributes exactly once.

examples.title: Verify the same row and column convention with scikit-learn
examples.explanationHtml: Rows are actual labels and columns are predicted labels, in the explicit order zero then one. A transposed matrix would swap the two error interpretations even if its diagonal looked unchanged.

examples.title: Read three-class errors on reserved iris flowers
examples.explanationHtml: The matrix expands to three rows and columns. Off-diagonal cells show which species are confused, rather than collapsing every mistake into one percentage. The model is fitted only on the training partition.

practice.title: Build a binary threshold matrix
practice.statementHtml: Read threshold from zero through one, then n from 1 to 30 and n lines score label. Scores must be finite in 0–1 and labels binary. Predict one at score ≥ threshold. Print tn, fp, fn and tp on labelled lines. Invalid input prints invalid.

practice.title: Build a three-class count matrix
practice.statementHtml: Read n from 1 to 30 and n actual/predicted integer label pairs from 0 through 2. Print the 3×3 count matrix with rows actual and columns predicted, one row per line. Invalid input prints invalid.
hints: Allocate all nine cells, including zero counts.
Increment only the selected row/column pair.

practice.title: Name the positive class before judging mistakes
practice.statementHtml: A classifier flags a message for review. Explain false positive and false negative after defining class one as unwanted message.
hints: Positive is a declared category, not a moral value.
practice.answerHtml: A false positive flags a normal message. A false negative misses an unwanted message. Their consequences differ, so state the positive class and action before deciding which mistake deserves more attention.

practice.title: Move a threshold without claiming new training
practice.statementHtml: Why can the confusion matrix change when the model weights and scores stay fixed?
practice.answerHtml: The threshold converts scores into labels. Moving it can change those labels while the score ranking stays fixed. Recount the four cells for the new policy; do not describe that alone as retraining or improved probability estimation.

quiz.prompt: Read actual-one, predicted-zero: which error and count does that cell show?
quiz.explanation: The example really belongs to class one but the decision missed it. Row meaning comes before column meaning.

caption.en: Six decisions with rows actual and columns predicted.
caption.bn: ছয়টি সিদ্ধান্তে row আসল ও column predicted লেবেল।

quiz.prompt: Read the three-class matrix: how many actual class-one examples were called class two?
quiz.explanation: Find row Actual 1 and column Pred 2. The entry is one; the mirrored error is a different cell.

caption.en: A three-class matrix with fixed label order.
caption.bn: নির্দিষ্ট লেবেলের ক্রমে তিন ক্লাস-এর matrix পড়ো।

quiz.prompt: Read the raised-threshold row: how many false positives remain?
quiz.explanation: The negative example scored 0.6 no longer passes 0.8. The two positive scores 0.8 and 0.9 still pass the inclusive cutoff.

caption.en: The same scores under two thresholds.
caption.bn: একই score-এ দুটি threshold-এর count দেখো।

quiz.prompt: What does positive mean in a binary matrix?
What changes when only a fixed-score threshold moves?
quiz.explanation: Scores can stay fixed while decisions change.

quiz.prompt: Which cells count exact binary label matches?
quiz.explanation: They lie on the actual/predicted diagonal.

quiz.prompt: What does a multiclass off-diagonal cell represent?
options: A probability guaranteed to sum to one
A specific actual class confused with a specific predicted class
quiz.explanation: Keep label order explicit on both axes.

quiz.prompt: Which cell is incremented for actual one and predicted zero?
quiz.explanation: Actual chooses row one and predicted chooses column zero.

quiz.prompt: How many total cases are in this binary matrix?
quiz.explanation: Every case belongs to exactly one cell, giving six.

quiz.prompt: Which decision follows score equality at threshold 0.8?
quiz.explanation: The inclusive threshold predicts one at equality.

keyPoints.en: Declare the positive class and the matrix axis convention.
keyPoints.bn: Positive ক্লাস ও matrix-এর অক্ষের অর্থ শুরুতেই বলো।

keyPoints.en: Actual labels choose rows and predicted labels choose columns here.
keyPoints.bn: এখানে আসল লেবেল row ও predicted লেবেল column বেছে দেয়।

keyPoints.en: False positives and false negatives describe different mistakes.
keyPoints.bn: False positive ও false negative দিয়ে দুই ধরনের ভুল বোঝায়।

keyPoints.en: Each evaluated example contributes to exactly one cell.
keyPoints.bn: যাচাইয়ের প্রতিটি উদাহরণ ঠিক একটি ঘরে গোনা হয়।

keyPoints.en: Moving a threshold can change decisions without refitting scores.
keyPoints.bn: Score আবার fit না করেও threshold সরিয়ে সিদ্ধান্ত বদলানো যায়।

examQuestions.question: Read TN=2, FP=1, FN=1 and TP=2: compute total and accuracy.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Total is 2+1+1+2=6. Correct predictions are TN+TP=4, so accuracy is 4/6≈0.667. The one false positive and one false negative remain different errors even though this percentage combines them.

examQuestions.question: Explain all four cells using an explicitly positive unwanted-message class.
examQuestions.answerHtml: TP flags an unwanted message correctly. TN leaves a normal message unflagged. FP flags a normal message, while FN misses an unwanted one. Which mistake is more costly depends on the review action and context; the class name alone does not decide that policy.

examQuestions.question: Explain what one off-diagonal entry means in a three-class matrix.
examQuestions.answerHtml: With rows actual and columns predicted, entry row one/column two counts actual class-one cases predicted as class two. Its mirror counts actual class-two cases predicted as one and can differ. A multiclass matrix reveals particular confusions that one accuracy number hides.
